findings_qualitative.value: Absorption against the central source, deepest at red-shifted velocity, may indicate infall

evidence.quote: The absorption features in the molecular lines towards the central bright source may indicate an infall.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular line emission is very inhomogeneous at small scales, which may indicate clumpiness in the disk

evidence.quote: The molecular line emission appears very inhomogeneous at small scales, which may indicate a small-scale clumpiness in the disk.

findings_qualitative.value: CH3CN near the NE2 and SW2 knots is shifted relative to C34S, suggesting C34S traces ambient gas and CH3CN also jet-entrained gas

evidence.quote: These features hint that the C$^{34}$S(7–6) emission arises mainly in the ambient gas

referee_caveats_inferred: Imaging and calibration settings are not given, so the 0.9 mm fluxes and the Gaussian-fit values cannot be checked against a reproduction
Free-free and dust decomposition relies on non-simultaneous literature fluxes at lower resolution
Keplerian curves are overlaid without a fit or uncertainty on M sin^2 i
Infall interpretation from absorption is qualitative
The Band 7 monitoring beam value quoted looks inconsistent and the data are not used

missing_for_reproduction: Imaging recipe (weighting, cell, size, masks, deconvolver)

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 100 GB to a few hundred GB raw for one 18.5-min execution with four 1.875 GHz windows at 1.13 MHz resolution, plus Band 7 monitoring data
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code and observing setup are given, but imaging parameters, region definitions and fitting software are absent, and the derived quantities rely on literature fluxes and rough estimates.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public status of the data is not stated and the imaging/analysis recipe is incomplete; main results are partly qualitative.
